children: fell about 15.5% at Wednesday's close as investors questioned whether debt-funded AI infrastructure projects can earn enough to justify their cost, while borrowing costs rose on its bonds.

Yields on CoreWeave's 9.625% notes due in 2032 reached 14.8%, while its 9.75% notes due in 2031 yielded about 14.9%. Bond yields rise when prices fall, showing lenders are seeking more compensation to hold its debt.

Chief Executive Mike Intrator said in a memo that CoreWeave's contracted backlog was sufficient to cover its debt obligations and dismissed the market reaction. Analysts, however, say its heavy borrowing and rapid data-center construction leave it more exposed than larger technology companies with stronger balance sheets.
The concern spread beyond CoreWeave. Oracle
dropped nearly 9% on Wednesday, while Nebius Group
and Dell Technologies (DELL) also declined as investors reassessed financing for the AI build-out. The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.9%.
Major cloud providers had issued more than $228 billion in bonds through Oct. 13, while AI infrastructure spending continues to expand, increasing scrutiny of future returns and financing costs.

title: CoreWeave Stock Crashes 15% as AI Debt Fears Rattle Wall Street
